NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Heavy rain has damaged many huts: fix them all in one day of work, or fix the worst first.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Three days of heavy rain have damaged half the huts in the village. (subject) wants the whole village to work together and fix every hut in one long day, singing. (friend) says some families have no roof at all and should come first. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The whole village works from dawn to dusk, hut to hut, singing the rebuilding song. By sunset every hut has a roof. Everyone is exhausted and covered in mud. It is a good day.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village fixes the roofless huts first. It takes a week to get to everyone. Some families with leaky roofs wait and grumble. The roofless families sleep dry from the first night.
